title: Paranormal activity found at abandoned CT hospital, investigators say. Spirits have 'had a lot to say.'
excerpt: Even after years of visits, she said, there is still more to learn about what may be happening inside the abandoned buildings.
content:
To Rose Porto, the Seaside Sanatorium evokes a deep sense of sadness, but as she gets closer to the historic abandoned buildings, she also feels as if she is being watched.

The founder of the CT Spirit Investigators said she can feel this energy around the former children’s tuberculosis hospital in Waterford and then a home for the elderly and later for the mentally disabled, which is said to be haunted by the many people who died there.

Porto says she has proof to back it up.

Her group has investigated the land surrounding the abandoned buildings many times in the 20 years since she began the paranormal research team. The group has reported shadows, voices, orbs and photographic anomalies during past visits. They have audio, photos and video to back up their findings.

Recently, while standing around the entrance to the main building, which is fenced in and covered in vines and graffiti, Porto takes out her spirit box. That’s a device used in paranormal investigations that rapidly scans radio frequencies, which investigators listen to for voices or responses they believe may be coming from spirits.

She places it on the ground and starts recording.

We came back to visit you. Do you want to talk to us? Are there any patients here that want to say hello? Are there any children here? Could you tell us your name, please?” Proto asks as the group of investigators listens in.

Although there are no responses over the static, in a recent visit, Porto and paranormal historian and researcher Jean Saccavino Garcia said that that they did have a visit from spirits they think were a bunch of children.

“The last two times we were here, and it sounded like it was a group of people that were here and they had a lot to say,” Porto said.

There also used to be swings in front of the building. Although they are no longer there, Porto said they have heard the creek of the swings before.

Seaside Sanatorium opened in 1934 as a hospital for children with tuberculosis, using sunlight and fresh sea air as part of their treatment. It was later converted into a geriatric hospital in 1959 and then the Seaside Regional Center, a residential facility for people with developmental disabilities, in 1961. The center closed in 1996 following reports of abuse and neglect. During the facility’s later years, some patients who died there were reportedly sent to the University of Connecticut for medical research, according to Garcia.

The property became Seaside State Park in 2014, but its buildings remain abandoned. For CT Spirit Investigators, the site’s history is part of its appeal.

Porto said her interest in the paranormal began when she was a child and had experiences she could not explain. As an adult, she joined local paranormal groups and learned different investigative techniques. She also received training through the Catholic Church in how to recognize and respond to suspected paranormal activity. Porto later founded CT Spirit Investigators and Researchers in 2003, turning her interest into a team that investigates homes, businesses and historic sites.

The group of seven does not charge people to investigate their homes as Porto said most of the time it is families who are having scary experiences in their homes and are asking for help.

“We don’t get paid for it. We all work regular jobs. And everything we do is donation. Some teams are putting a price tag on it, but we don’t. We never have. We probably never will. It’s just taking money from families that are already in terrible situations. We don’t want to put more of a burden on them,” Porto said.

Porto said the groups have investigated homes where residents reported unexplained noises, strange activity and a feeling that something was in the house. In one case, a family felt uncomfortable changing anything in their home because they felt they were not really the owners. During an investigation, the team said it witnessed a dog appear to be struck by an unseen force and later heard a loud bang while investigating the basement. Porto said the group tries to find logical explanations for what people experience before considering paranormal causes.

“By the time they call us, they have like a really serious incident happen, and they want answers,” Porto said.

During a recent investigation at Brookside Farm Museum in East Lyme, the CT Spirit Investigators said they heard children’s voices, footsteps and saw shadows inside the house. Porto said the team believed there were two children and heard the older child tell the younger one to hide when Garcia entered the room.

The investigators also reported feeling something brush against their legs and a cold breeze, which they believed could have been a spirit cat as they found out later that previous owner had a cat. The team said its REM pod, a device that alerts investigators to movement or disturbances nearby, went off as they heard footsteps in the barn. One investigator also reported that a book flew off a stack during the investigation.

Porto said some investigations can be dangerous, particularly when the team believes it is dealing with a demonic presence rather than what it considers a human spirit.

She said many people don’t know what they are dealing with when they think a spirit is in their home. Porto said she has handled cases involving what she described as demonic activity that she cannot talk about publicly. When her own attempts to clear a home do not work, she said the team may call in a Catholic priest to help.

“Sometimes spirits can show themselves as anything they want to, and that’s the problem,” Porto said. “People think they’re talking to a little child or they think they’re talking to their grandmother. When indeed it’s like the demonic energy.

Most people call Porto because they want the spirit removed from their home as it is causing them problems and they can’t live normally.

Before beginning an investigation, Porto said, she interviews people multiple times and may visit their homes to determine whether further investigation is needed. She said some callers may be seeking attention, so the team tries to rule out those possibilities and find logical explanations for reported activity before moving forward.

The team also researches a location’s history and spends several visits there to see whether the reported activity happens again. Porto said some investigations find answers after just a few visits, while others can continue for years because the team may not experience anything unusual right away or it takes years to get rid of the spirit. One of their investigations went on for 10 years.

Once the team believes it has identified what is happening, it decides how to proceed. Porto said people can unintentionally bring spirits home after participating in séances or other paranormal activities. If the team believes a home needs to be cleared, she first tries to perform a clearing through prayers. If that does not work, the team brings in a priest, particularly in cases it considers more severe.

Porto said the team keeps returning to locations like Seaside because paranormal investigations can take time, and experiences are not always easy to explain. Even after years of visits, she said, there is still more to learn about what may be happening inside the abandoned buildings.

More information about the CT Spirit Investigators can be found on their website, https://ctspiritinvestigators.com.
